Recalibrating the Newlyn tide gauge

The Newlyn gauge has anchored the British vertical datum since 1915, and its drift is now large enough to matter for the flood models that depend on it.

Recalibration ran over three spring tides. The correction is small, a little under four millimetres a year, but it is systematic, and a systematic error in a reference gauge propagates into every derived level in the network.

What changed

The benchmark tie was re-surveyed and the stilling well cleared. Readings from the redundant radar sensor were used to bracket the float record.
